top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice is a new physical principle for neutral atoms, distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It has been reproduced and cross-compared at the 1e-18 level by independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE), which answers my questions about confirmation and systematics. Katori for the scheme and first lattice clock and Ye for accuracy and many-body control is the cleanest two-name allocation on the slate. The topological insulator proposals are scientifically mature but carry a contested third seat and the unresolved Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit. Between them I prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, because Kane and Mele are joint originators of the 2005 theory and the citation can be limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and its HgTe observation. Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan comes next, since it separates Mele from Kane. Any award is preferable to no award, given a mature, independently confirmed candidate.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for the clock or topological insulator proposals: PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur work is unconnected. As chair I disclosed support for P002 in round 2 and this ballot should be discounted accordingly.
